subject: physics_2
question_text: Give any one use of infrared rays.

mark_split.label: One use of infrared rays, stated fully

verification.note: The single 2-mark step is an INVENTED split and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: the book (p.41) lists four uses — solar water heaters or cookers, photographs in fog and smoke, infrared lamps in physical therapy, and remote switches of household TV and video recorders — all genuine infrared applications; the question asks for any one, so one complete use carries the full 2 marks and the rest are alternatives.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: One use of infrared rays
steps.mark_note: Any one correct use, in a full sentence
lines: Infrared rays are used in solar water
steps.margin_note: Full marks for any one correct use written as a complete sentence.
steps.why: Infrared radiation carries heat, so every use on the book's list is a heating or heat-sensing job. Writing the use as a full sentence, with the device named, is what the examiner marks.
common_mistakes: Writing only the word heating with no device. Name a device or a situation, such as solar water heaters.
Giving a use of ultraviolet rays, such as sterilising water. The question asks about infrared.

recall.must_convey: Any one correct use of infrared rays, such as solar water heaters or solar cookers.

steps.memory_tip: Infrared means heat: pick the heater or the cooker and say it as one sentence.

steps.margin_note: Any one of these earns the same two marks; you do not need more than one.
steps.why: The book prints four uses so that any one of them can be written in the exam. Knowing the list gives you a spare answer if one use slips from memory in the hall.
common_mistakes: Writing all four uses in the exam. One complete use is enough for the two marks; the rest only costs time.

recall.must_convey: A second use of infrared rays from the book's list, as a backup.

steps.memory_tip: Four uses: heaters and cookers, fog photographs, therapy lamps, remotes.

insider_note: The question says any one use — one complete sentence earns both marks; a bare word like heating does not.
